# Education in Sweden
Education in Sweden is organized into several levels: preschool (Förskola, ages 1–6), a compulsory nine-year comprehensive school (Grundskola, ages 7–16), and upper secondary education (Gymnasieskola, ages 16–19). Preschool is offered to children from age one when parents are working or studying, and from age three, every child is entitled to three hours of preschool for free. Grundskola covers primary and lower secondary education and is mandatory between ages six–seven and fifteen–sixteen, consisting of 16 compulsory subjects and additional language options. Grading is provided from year 6, with students evaluated using a letter system from A to F. Upon completion, students apply to upper secondary school, which is elective but has a 99% enrollment rate. Upper secondary is divided into 18 national programmes–preparatory and vocational–with admission based on grades and specific subject requirements.
Higher education comprises public universities, university colleges, and higher vocational schools. Swedish academic degrees align with the Bologna Process: Bachelor's level (three years), Master's level (one or two years), and Doctoral level (two to four years). Admission typically requires completion of upper secondary education and demonstrated proficiency in Swedish and English. Sweden also offers independent "free" schools (friskolor), which are publicly funded but run privately and account for approximately 15% of primary and 30% of upper secondary enrollments as of 2023. While Swedish education is tuition-free for Swedish, EU/EEA, and Swiss citizens, financial aid is available to all students. Sweden participates actively in international educational assessments such as PISA and PIRLS and has implemented regular guidelines to improve educational quality and prevent discrimination.
